caption: Overview of MobileJudgeBench . We construct a judge benchmark from 931 human-annotated mobile agent trajectories spanning 6 benchmarks (left, § 3 ), evaluate 6 LLM-as-judge methods across 5 backends (middle, § 5.1 ), and validate that benchmark metrics predict judge utility for agent evaluation (§ 5.2.1 ) and on-policy training (§ 5.2.2 ), complemented by a root-cause failure analysis (§ 5.3 ) (right).

Benchmark statistics. Tasks are unique task definitions; trajectories include up to 4 agent runs per task. Total app count excludes cross-app task categories in SPA-Bench; some apps appear in multiple benchmarks.

Judge accuracy (%) across methods and LLM backends (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, GPT-5-mini, Gemini 3 Flash, GLM-4.6V, Claude Sonnet 4.5). Bold marks the best backend per method (row-wise); underline marks the best method per backend (column-wise). Full results in Appendix D . † Default configuration: 48 uniformly sampled screenshots at max long edge 600px; no UI metadata or agent reasoning; see ablation below.

Ablation study on simple baseline judge. Top: fewer higher-resolution screenshots outperform many low-resolution ones at equal cost. Bottom: UI metadata has minimal impact; agent reasoning provides a modest gain for GPT only.

Meta-correlation across 30 judge variants. Each cell is the Spearman ρ s \rho_{s} between a judge quality metric and a reliability metric: agent ranking fidelity ( ρ s \rho_{s} w/ Ranking) or success-rate estimation error ( ρ s \rho_{s} w/ MAE, where negative means higher quality → \to lower error). Brackets give 95% CIs from a task-cluster bootstrap (tasks resampled with replacement within each source benchmark; 2,000 replicates; the 30 judge variants held fixed). Bold marks the strongest predictor per column.

Judge quality predicts evaluation reliability (30 method × \times backend variants; marker shape = = judge method, color = = LLM backend). (a) Balanced accuracy correlates with agent ranking fidelity ( ρ s = 0.87 \rho_{s}{=}0.87 ). (b) Balanced accuracy inversely correlates with success-rate estimation error. (c) The highest-accuracy judge (Baseline/Gemini, 90.9%) closely tracks human success rates across 24 agents ( ρ = 0.97 \rho{=}0.97 ).

On-policy RL training curves with different judge reward signals (mean ± \pm std over 3 seeds). Inset table: judge quality on the AndroidWorld subset (Acc/Prec/Rec %) and best easy-set success rate. Training performance tracks judge accuracy (rule-based > > GPT-5-mini > > {GPT-5.2, Qwen}); the equal-accuracy pair is ordered by precision under the best-checkpoint convention.

Root cause taxonomy for hard-core failures. The GPT set is dominated by false negatives (last-frame anchoring, unfamiliar success state), while the Qwen set is dominated by false positives (constraint violation, partial completion). Surface UI match is a shared weakness across both backends.

Annotation platform. Left: trajectory video view with task description, agent reasoning, and playback controls. Center: step-by-step viewer showing before/after screenshots and action details. Right: annotation form collecting task achievability, success, optimality, side effects, repetition cycles, and free-text notes.

Structured comparison of AgentRewardBench ( 23 ) and MobileJudgeBench . The two benchmarks cover different agent domains and are complementary; MobileJudgeBench additionally validates judge metrics against downstream evaluation and training utility.

The 24 agent-level data points used for computing ranking fidelity and rate estimation error. Rate is the human-annotated success rate. Agents are grouped by model and sorted by success rate within each group.

Full evaluation results for all 30 judge variants, sorted by accuracy. Acc/Prec/Rec/F1/BAcc are trajectory-level percentages. Ag. ρ \rho is the agent-level Spearman rank correlation with human rankings. Ag.MAE is the mean absolute error of per-agent success rate estimates.

Task-cluster bootstrap 95% CIs for the meta-correlation across the 30 judge variants. Green: interval excludes zero; grey: interval spans zero. Precision is non-predictive for both reliability metrics.

Share of total variance ( η 2 \eta^{2} ) across the 6 × \times 5 judge grid attributable to the method and backbone main effects and the residual (interaction), with task-cluster bootstrap 95% CIs. The lower block repeats the decomposition on the competitive 4 × \times 5 subgrid that excludes the two A3 modes; the same task draws are used for both grids.
Training hyperparameters for on-policy RL experiments.
Success rate (%) on the complete 116-task AndroidWorld suite, averaged over 3 seeds: best checkpoint per condition vs. the final (step-300) checkpoint.
Per-seed easy-set accuracy for each reward condition. Seed variance is moderate; the ranking Rule-based > > GPT-5-mini > > GPT-5.2 > > Qwen is consistent across most seeds and steps.
Representative false negative failure examples (4 categories). Judges incorrectly predict failure despite task success.
Representative false positive failure examples (3 categories). Judges incorrectly predict success despite task failure.
